name: @pinecall/mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The org this API key belongs to — name, slug, plan/tier and remaining credits.

tools.name: set_api_key
tools.description: Store a Pinecall API key (pk_...) for this MCP session — in memory, or with persist:true also in ~/.pinecall/credentials (0600). Never echoed back.

key.description: The Pinecall API key, e.g. pk_live_… — it is never echoed back

persist.description: Also save it to ~/.pinecall/credentials (mode 0600) so future sessions and the CLI find it

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the Pinecall documentation (semantic, no LLM). Returns the top matching doc chunks with their path.

query.description: What you want to know, in natural language, e.g. 'call log cursor'

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Read a whole Pinecall docs page as markdown, by the path docs_search returned (e.g. guides/call-log).

path.description: The doc path from a docs_search hit, e.g. guides/call-log (the .md is optional)

tools.name: knowledge
tools.description: Knowledge bases (RAG): list the org's KBs, query one for ranked chunks, or push documents into one.

action.description: list the org's KBs · query one · push documents into one

kb.description: Knowledge base id (24-hex) or exact name. Optional when the org has exactly one KB.

query.description: action=query: the question — semantic search, no LLM

docs.description: action=push: the documents, content included — this server never reads local files

path.description: Stable identifier, e.g. docs/pricing.md — push is idempotent by path

content.description: The document text (markdown or plain text)

title.description: Human title; defaults to the path's basename

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: The org's agents with their online state, channels and phone numbers — who exists and who is running right now.

tools.name: configure_agent
tools.description: Create or hot-reload a DEV agent (slug must start with dev-) and hold it live for this session, so chat and calls can reach it.

slug.description: Agent id. MUST start with "dev-" — production slugs are refused.

language.description: ISO language code, e.g. "es". Affects STT and TTS model defaults.

greeting.description: Spoken/sent on every inbound call before the user says anything.

phoneNumber.description: E.164 number this dev agent should answer on (see list_phones). It is released when the session ends.

tools.name: run_agent
tools.description: Run your project's agent entry file as a managed child process (like `pinecall run`), so an agent with code tools is live and chattable. Also stop/status/logs.

file.description: Path to your agent entry file, relative to the project root — e.g. "agent/index.mjs" or "src/agent.ts". Required for action "start".

lines.description: For action "logs": how many trailing lines (default 50).

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Send a text message to a Pinecall agent and return its reply. Continue a conversation by passing the session id back. Read-only: chat never mutates an agent.

agent.description: Agent slug, e.g. dev-support or the production slug

message.description: What to say to the agent, as a caller would say it

session.description: Session id returned by a previous chat call — continues that conversation with its history

timeoutSeconds.description: Budget for this turn, connect included (default 30s)

tools.name: list_phones
tools.description: Every phone number in the org with its assignment (agent slug or free), whether that agent is live, and any dev- routing override.

free.description: Only the unassigned numbers — the ones safe to claim.

tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: Calls of one agent — id, live?, direction, from, started/ended — newest first. The index into the call log; read one with get_call.

tools.name: get_call
tools.description: One call's log, reduced: phase, transcript messages with seqs, tool calls with args and results, turn latencies, summary. Cursor-paged with after/nextAfter.

call_id.description: Call id, e.g. CA4cbc... — from list_calls.

after.description: Resume cursor: the nextAfter of the previous page.

agent.description: Agent slug, if known — skips resolving it.

tools.name: observe
tools.description: Live tail of the call log as a long poll: waits until something happens, then returns it. With agent — the whole job in one loop: it answers when a call starts, carrying the call id AND its first entries, then keeps streaming that call's transcript on the next calls, and goes back to waiting when it ends. With call_id — the same tail for one known call. Silence returns timedOut, never an error.

call_id.description: Tail exactly this call. Usually unnecessary: observe(agent) follows the live call by itself.

agent.description: Agent slug to tail — catches a call starting and then streams it. Also skips resolving the agent for call_id.

after.description: Resume cursor: the nextAfter of the previous observe. Omit on the first call to start from now.

call_after.description: Agent mode, optional: cursor into the followed call's log. Omit — it is tracked for you and returned as callAfter.

waitSeconds.description: How long to hold the poll open with nothing happening (default 25s, max 50s).

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: The models the server accepts for a kind (llm | stt | tts), each with the exact config shortcut string and notes (languages, managed vs BYOK, realtime).

kind.description: llm, stt or tts — which agent-config field you are filling.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: TTS voices with the exact `voice` config string (e.g. "elevenlabs/sarah"), filterable by provider and language.

provider.description: One TTS provider. Omitted: every managed provider is queried.

language.description: ISO language code prefix, e.g. "es" — matches es, es-ES, es-419.

tools.name: play_voice
tools.description: Play a sample of a TTS voice out loud on this machine, so you can pick a `voice` by ear (stdio MCP only).

voice.description: The exact `voice` string from list_voices, e.g. "elevenlabs/sarah".

text.description: What the voice should say. Only honoured on providers the server synthesizes previews for (rime, xai); a provider-hosted preview clip is fixed.

language.description: ISO language code for a synthesized sample, e.g. "es".

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: The org's plan and credits, the plan catalogue, and a Stripe link the human opens to subscribe, upgrade or manage billing.

plan.description: Plan name to move to, e.g. starter / pro / enterprise. Omit to just report the current plan and hand back the billing-portal link.

tools.name: byok
tools.description: Bring your own provider key: list which providers the org has a key for, set one, or remove one. Keys are never returned.

provider.description: Provider name, e.g. deepgram, gladia, cartesia, elevenlabs, xai, groq…

key.description: The provider's own API key. Sent to Pinecall once and never echoed back.

instructions:
# Pinecall MCP — zero to a production voice agent

## The journey

1. `whoami` — proves the key, names the org. No key? `set_api_key`.
2. Read the docs for what you are building (below). Never guess a shape.
3. Pick from the live catalog, not memory: `list_models`, `list_voices` (+ `play_voice`), `list_phones`.
4. `configure_agent`, `dev-` slug only. Registering HOT-RELOADS the live agent, so a prod
   slug clobbers the process owning it — and its reconnect clobbers you back.
5. Iterate with `chat`; it never mutates, so prod is safe to chat.
   **Chat IS the testing story** — no test-runner tool: spec testing is deliberately disabled.
6. Wire a number: a free `list_phones` row as `phoneNumber`.
7. Debug: `list_calls` → `get_call`.

Ground with `knowledge`, survey with `list_agents`, ship via `pc.agent(...)`.

## Read before you write

`docs_search` locates a page, `get_doc` reads it whole. Start from:
first agent → `quickstart` + `guides/build-a-live-call-app` · phone → `guides/inbound-voice`,
`guides/outbound-calls` · WhatsApp → `guides/whatsapp` · tools → `guides/tools-and-functions` ·
browser voice/chat → `web/widget/overview`, `web/chat/overview` · call log → `guides/call-log` ·
multi-tenant → `guides/multi-tenant`.

## Not here — say so, do not fake it

- No outbound dialling, no account creation (pinecall.io); `play_voice` needs stdio speakers.
- Never print an API key. Page with `after`.

## The tools

### whoami

Call it FIRST — the auth probe; a 401 means every tool fails the same. `keySource` names where the key came from; on `shell-rc` relay the `notice`.

### set_api_key

Only when discovery found no key. `persist: true` also writes ~/.pinecall/credentials (0600, CLI-shared) — ask first. `verified: false` = stored but failing.

### docs_search

It locates; `get_doc` reads. Nearest-neighbour: a `score` near 1.0 clear of the rest is real, a flat ~0.8 run means the docs do not cover it.

### get_doc

Read whole pages before coding: a snippet is 400 chars of one chunk, without imports or caveats. Unknown path → `suggestions`.

### knowledge

RAG. Attach with `knowledgeBase: "<kbId>"`; chunks auto-inject, or place `{{RAG_CONTEXT}}`. `push` takes content YOU read, idempotent by `path`, reindexed automatically.

### list_agents

`online: true` means a live process owns that agent — reconfiguring it is a clobber. Only `dev: true` slugs are yours; `devOverrides` = phone → dev agent.

### configure_agent

A re-configure REPLACES the config: resend every field you still want. Non-`dev-` refused; `heldBySession` for this session. No `tools` param — code tools need an SDK process (`run_agent` / `pinecall run`, `docs_search` it). `phoneNumber` is verified against live routing: the server refuses (`PHONE_IN_USE`) a number another dev agent holds, so `routed:false` + `routedTo` means take a free `list_phones` number. Relay `dialThisNumber`; never invite a call when it is null.

### run_agent

The loop: write agent code → start → `chat` → `logs` when a reply is off → `stop`. Needed when the agent has code tools (`configure_agent` cannot carry functions). ONE process per session; killed when this server exits. SECURITY: runs YOUR project's code locally with your key in its env — IDE-terminal trust, files inside cwd only.

### chat

The testing path — there is no test-runner tool. Converse: ask what a real caller would and judge the transcript. The returned `session` id IS the thread: pass it back to continue; each reply is matched to your message (`in_reply_to`); 15 min idle.

### list_phones

`agent: null` is the only free number. A stored `agent` with `live: false` is owned-but-offline, NOT free: a second agent steals its calls.

### list_calls

The lifecycle index, no transcripts: find the `call` id of what just happened, then read it with `get_call`.

### get_call

The debugger: read the log instead of guessing. `truncated` → call again with `after = nextAfter`; `gaps` = the hot buffer moved past you.

### observe

The live debugger: call `observe(agent)` in a loop, passing back `nextAfter` each time, and nothing else — it waits for a call to start, hands you `call` with its first entries, then streams that call's transcript, then waits again. `timedOut: true` means nothing happened: call again with the SAME cursor. `following` says which log it is on. `get_call` for a finished transcript.

### list_models

Paste `shortcut` verbatim (`provider/model`; bare = OpenAI). Pick STT by language: `deepgram/flux` is the default but ~20 languages (no Arabic, Hindi, Thai, Urdu) — else `nova-3`/`soniox/realtime`. Pick only `usable: true`: `managed: false` = BYOK, and a `usable: false` row needs `byok('set', provider, key)` before it will run.

### list_voices

Use the `voice` string verbatim — the alias is not the provider's raw id. Filter by `language`/`provider`; BYOK ones must be named. Prefer `usable: true` — a `usable: false` row needs `byok('set', provider, key)` first.

### play_voice

Pick a row from `list_voices` and pass its `voice` verbatim. Audio leaves the USER's speakers: say so first. ElevenLabs/Cartesia return a fixed clip, so `text` is ignored; `played: false` → give the `previewUrl`.

### subscribe

No-arg = read-only: plan, credits, catalogue, `portalUrl` (Stripe portal; null until the org has ever paid — normal). With `plan`: `checkoutUrl` for a first subscription, but an EXISTING subscriber is switched in place with proration — a real billing change, ask the human first. Hand URLs over verbatim; never touch or request card data; expired link → call again.

### byok

Bring-your-own provider keys: `list` (never key material), `set`, `remove`. BYOK bills the org's OWN provider account and flips `managed: false` models on — tradeoffs: get_doc('reference/managed-vs-byok'). The submitted key transits once and is scrubbed from every output.
